title: Kitchen and Promise
premise: Emrys Brightwater, once a celebrated wedding planner, retreated to a small coastal town after a betrayal she has never fully explained to anyone, including herself. When a letter postmarked eleven years ago surfaces in her late mother's belongings, it forces her to confront the fiancé she abandoned at the altar and the truth about why she ran. Hired to plan one final wedding before the season ends, Emrys discovers the groom is the man whose life she shattered. Through the weeks of preparations, old loyalties and buried truths collide, and on the night of the last ferry, Emrys must choose between fleeing again or staying to claim the life—and the love—she once refused.
about_author: Noor Iversen is a former pastry chef turned novelist who writes love stories set in kitchens, harbors, and the quiet hours between them. She lives on a windswept island where the ferries keep imperfect time, much like her characters.

chapters.title: The Weight of White Sugar
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Three years into her careful new life, Emrys runs a modest bakery-café and takes only small catering jobs, refusing all wedding work. A routine order for a bridal shower rattles her more than she admits. Emotional beat: the fragile calm of a woman who has mistaken avoidance for peace.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Clearing her late mother's attic, Emrys finds an unopened letter addressed to her, postmarked the week after she fled her own wedding. She cannot bring herself to read it. Emotional beat: dread and longing tangled together; the past knocking politely at the door.

chapters.title: A Commission in Salt Air
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. A wealthy client insists Emrys plan her daughter's wedding—the last big event before the ferry season closes. Desperate for money to save the café, Emrys accepts, then learns the groom's name: Callum Reeve, the man she left waiting. Emotional beat: panic disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: What Callum Kept
chapters.summary: POV: Callum. Callum requested Emrys deliberately, carrying his own unanswered questions about that morning eleven years ago. He tells himself it's closure he wants, not revenge. Their first meeting is brittle, courteous, electric. Emotional beat: a man discovering that anger was only ever grief wearing armor.

chapters.title: Tasting Menus and Old Wounds
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Wedding planning forces long days side by side: menu tastings, florists, seating charts. Small kindnesses erode Emrys's defenses, and she finally reads the letter—her mother's confession about the family debt and shame that drove the flight. Emotional beat: grief reframed as understanding.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal Nobody Planned
chapters.summary: POV: Callum. At a storm-delayed rehearsal dinner, Callum's mother confronts Emrys publicly with the old accusation. Callum defends her—too fiercely, revealing how much he still cares. The bride-to-be quietly wonders if her wedding is built on someone else's unfinished story. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against truth.

chapters.title: Breadcrumbs
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Emrys uncovers evidence that Callum's best man engineered the original catastrophe—a forged note, a stolen deposit—as part of an old grudge. Telling Callum means admitting how completely she misjudged him. Emotional beat: courage gathering like a tide; forgiveness of others beginning with self-forgiveness.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. On the empty beach, Emrys tells Callum everything: the debt, the forged note, the shame that made invisibility feel like safety. He confesses he requested her hoping to rekindle what was lost. They kiss, then pull apart—he is still promised to another woman's wedding day. Emotional beat: the climax of honesty, and its cost.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. The wedding proceeds beautifully under Emrys's flawless planning—but the bride, seeing the truth, releases Callum from vows neither of them believes in. As the season's final ferry sounds its horn, Emrys stands at the dock with a ticket in hand, deciding whether invisible is who she wants to be. Emotional beat: the hinge of choice.

chapters.title: Kitchen and Promise
chapters.summary: POV: Emrys. Emrys tears up the ticket. In her café kitchen, flour-dusted and unhidden, she and Callum make a small private promise—not a wedding, just a beginning: breakfast tomorrow, and every honest day after. Emotional beat: belonging found not in grand ceremonies but in staying, visible and forgiven.
